review: Independent source baseline; no code changes, simulator execution, or physical-device validation

confirmed_findings.evidence: AudioService is @MainActor. ensureOutput (495-497) and restartOutput (550-562) call configureSession (469-472), which calls AudioSessionOwner.activate (1224-1227). activate synchronously waits on the serial session queue across category, sample-rate, buffer and setActive calls (1257-1289). An in-flight deactivation on that queue adds to the wait. This is a real synchronous UI-blocking path, although historical 9.4s and 2.2s measurements were not reproduced in this review.
confirmed_findings.proposal: Use the existing serial session queue through activateInBackground, keeping AVAudioEngine graph changes on its existing main actor. Add a cancellable, generation-checked output-start coordinator with explicit starting/ready/failed completion; reserve output intent before awaiting. Coalesce simultaneous engine starts. Preserve live renderer state when capture and output share an engine. Never merely wrap ensureOutput in a fire-and-forget Task: stop/newer settings/interruption must invalidate pending work and take clocks must wait for readiness.
confirmed_findings.timing_dependency: SongPerform.startMelody:525 starts click before session.begin, while Highway.start:747 begins session before click at 755. SongChords, RhythmStep, SongSheet and LatencyCalibration also need startup-order review. A delayed async click must not let count-in, judging, cue or band clocks advance before engine startup completes; readiness must be awaited or delivered to a guarded callback before clock initialization. Keep observed render-origin correction afterward.

confirmed_findings.evidence: interruptionBegan:615 snapshots and calls suspend. stop:437 also only calls suspend, which does not clear interrupted. interruptionEnded:621 restores that saved snapshot unconditionally when shouldResume. Thus user stop/navigation during a call can be undone when the call ends; microphone/drone/tool click can restart after explicit stop.
confirmed_findings.proposal: Separate transient interruption suspension from explicit intent cancellation. An explicit stop clears saved restore intent or advances a lifecycle token that restore must match. A stopCapture should independently remove microphone intent from any pending interruption snapshot without cancelling a desired background tool click.

confirmed_findings.evidence: snapshot:586 only captures running && tapInstalled. An interruption while start awaits permission/session activation has captureWanted=true but running=false, so suspend cancels generation and discards requested capture without preserving it for shouldResume. Tuner scene activation may incidentally retry but that is not a reliable lifecycle guarantee for lesson capture.
confirmed_findings.proposal: Represent desired capture settings as explicit state before asynchronous startup; snapshot valid desired capture, not only the installed tap. Gate automatic restore on current owner/lifecycle intent and application foreground state. Avoid snapshotting unfinished user settings from the previous capture.

confirmed_findings.evidence: rebuild:546 and restore:603 enqueue Task { await listen(capture) } without checking an intent token inside the new task. A stop between task creation and execution increments generation but listen/start begins a new generation anyway. stopTone:739 already demonstrates the needed token check.
confirmed_findings.proposal: Capture and revalidate an intent/lifecycle token inside every delayed restore/rebuild task before calling start, and revalidate after each await.

historical_notes_already_addressed_in_ba: Microphone session activation already runs off-main via activateInBackground.

activationsPending:59, 259-276 and shutdown:464 prevent a stale microphone completion from releasing the single .lessons holder while a newer activation is pending. If a newer capture already runs, running prevents release. The older stale-release note is not evidence that this exact defect remains.
MicStartRetry already retries selected transient failures once with 300ms delay; tests cover classification, not async ownership behavior.

Band rendering already uses userInitiated; attack-graded speaker-band exclusion and hardware-rate rerender are present according to current code/docs. Their actual acoustic behavior remains unvalidated.

Route/config notifications already coalesce over 180ms, compare input signature, preserve renderer state, and filter other engines' configuration changes. Do not replace these with unconditional independent restarts.
TuneView scenePhase active calls autoListen, so plain tuner background/foreground is not solely dependent on AudioService.resumeWhenActive.
other_review_observations: AudioSessionOwner still tracks one holder per user, not a per-request lease. An async output migration must include all new pending output activations in shutdown ownership protection or replace holder tracking with generation-specific leases; otherwise it reintroduces the stale release race that activationsPending currently prevents for microphone only.

prepareInterfaceSound also queue.sync waits at 1322 even though its comment says never waits on deactivation. Holders are inserted only after configure succeeds, so a pending first background activation leaves a window where interface-sound preparation can wait on that queue. Include in nonblocking-session audit.

RecordingPlayer.engineStopped sets isPlaying=false and releases the session but does not restart. Its class comment claims it plays on after a route/session configuration change. This discrepancy merits a targeted playback route test; source alone does not establish notification order or a safe unconditional restart during interruptions.
An interruption shouldResume snapshot is only a hint to restore still-desired playback. Never use it to bypass explicit user stop.
meaningful_regression_tests: Inject a session activator with a manually suspended continuation; verify a main-actor heartbeat advances while output startup is suspended, then engine startup occurs only after activation succeeds.

Delay activation A, issue stop and start B, finish A/B in both orders; no stale renderer/tap restart, no stale error, no session release while B is pending or running. Finish a cancelled-only activation and require exactly one cleanup release.
Start metronome then stop while activation is pending; completion must not produce a click. Update tempo/voice while pending; newest settings win and only one engine startup occurs.

Keep drone/tool click active while capture is cancelled or fails; capture cleanup must not release active output. Keep capture active while output stop/start occurs; input tap remains valid and output does not duplicate graph nodes.

Suspend activation then send interruption began/end; resume still-requested capture on shouldResume only. Explicit stop/navigation during interruption suppresses restore. No shouldResume leaves stopped. A scheduled rebuild task cannot restart after explicit stop.

Inject an engine-ready gate into lesson startup. Take/session/cue clocks remain unstarted until click readiness, including delayed and failed activation; band firstBar is scheduled after the same ready point.

Existing MicStartRetryTests exercise only retry policy. TunerSessionTests exercise tuner state; neither tests AudioService/AudioSessionOwner lifecycle. No direct AudioService/AudioSessionOwner/SessionInterruption test references were found in TimbreAppTests at baseline.

Use an injected AVAudioSession facade and controllable serial executor/grace clock to test pending release cancellation and startup ordering rather than assertions that mirror arithmetic counters. Keep a smaller app-host integration test for graph lifecycle; a pure core policy test alone cannot prove actual callers use it.

physical_device_release_gate.required: Run all 12 AUDIO-DEVICE-TESTS cases on real devices; include 2-3 iPhones and one iPad as KNOWN-ISSUES requests, speaker/AirPods/wired routes, Low Power Mode, permission denied, quick stop/restart and drone+mic. Record hardware, iOS, build, timing, heard behavior and logs.
specific_limits: Off-main activation removes a known synchronous UI wait but does not prove AVAudioEngine.start cannot itself block.
Speaker drum bleed/strum grading, silent switch, haptics while recording, Bluetooth latency/rate changes and call/Siri recovery need real hardware.
Measure Perform-to-first-click and main-thread responsiveness; any freeze above the documented 300ms threshold remains a release failure.
No hardware pass or App Store readiness claim follows from static review or simulator tests.
